name: Hange-koboku-to (Kampo formula; banxia houpo tang in Chinese; also called Banha-Hubak-Tang)
short: Pregnancy: no data on this formula alone; its herb Pinellia: embryo deaths in rats. Liver injury: 1 title-only case, different combined formula. Trials (elderly; depression): no severe adverse events.
text: Names and herbs: a 1999 trial abstract gives Hange Koboku-To as the Japanese name of Banxia Houpo Tang; a laboratory abstract gives banxia-houpo-tang for hangekobokuto and lists its five herbs as Pinellia tuber, Poria, magnolia bark, perilla herb and ginger; and a 2023 review of this East Asian formula gives Banha-Hubak-Tang as another name for it (the abstract does not say in which language). Trials: in a 12-month observer-blinded randomized trial in 95 elderly patients with dementia in two Japanese long-term care hospitals, comparing the formula (spelled banxia houpu tang in that abstract) with placebo, no adverse events were observed from the formula; pneumonia, the outcome the trial measured, developed in 4 people on the formula (1 of whom died) and 14 on placebo (6 of whom died). A 2023 meta-analysis of 15 randomized trials (1,714 participants with depression) found that the formula alone had a lower risk of adverse events than antidepressants alone and a similar risk when combined with them; no severe adverse events were reported, but the overall risk of bias was high and the quality of evidence very low to moderate. Liver: a 1997 case report, available as a title only, describes drug-induced liver injury due to bukuryo-in-go-hange-koboku-to (as titled), a different product whose name includes this formula's; the title gives no further details. Pregnancy: no study of this formula on its own in pregnancy was found. Two Japanese database studies (observational) pooled it with other Kampo medicines and give no result for it alone: among 121,287 mothers in a study of hyperemesis gravidarum, congenital anomalies, low birthweight and preterm birth did not differ significantly among the groups, and among 179,707 mothers in a study of depression in pregnancy, adverse neonatal outcomes did not differ significantly between women given Kampo medicines and women without depression. The formula contains Pinellia tuber; in a study in pregnant rats, crude Pinellia powder increased vaginal bleeding and embryo deaths, processed powder at the same dose showed no toxicity, and a decoction of processed or crude rhizome at a higher dose increased both (animal data; the cited abstracts do not say whether the Pinellia in this formula is processed). Lungs (reporting data): in an analysis of Japan's adverse-drug-event reports on herbal medicines (the abstract does not name this formula), daily intake of its herb Pinellia tuber was associated with reports of drug-induced interstitial lung disease, a severe adverse event, with an adjusted reporting odds ratio of 1.05 (95% CI 1.01 to 1.10) for daily intake (the abstract does not give the unit), and the authors conclude that the lung disease was dose-dependent on the crude drugs; reporting data of this kind cannot show cause. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
